elements.element: The exit obligations apply upon both expiry and termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3 applies “Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason.”
Section 10.3(a) requires Vendor, at Customer's request, to “provide reasonable transition assistance.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3(a) expressly provides assistance “for up to six (6) months.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must be provided at then-current rates.

elements.evidence: Section 10.3(b) requires Vendor to “return all Customer Data.”

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3(b) requires return “within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination.”

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3(b) expressly requires “a standard machine-readable format.”

elements.element: Vendor must delete Customer Data after returning it.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3(c) requires Vendor to “thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems.”

elements.element: Vendor must certify deletion after deleting Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3(c) requires Vendor to “certify such deletion in writing.”

elements.element: The fallback exit obligations apply upon both expiry and termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3 is triggered upon “expiry or termination” of the Agreement or any Order Form.
Section 10.3(a) requires reasonable transition assistance at Customer's request.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for 90 days.
elements.evidence: The stated period of up to six months encompasses the required 90-day fallback period.
The obligation to return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format constitutes a data export obligation.

elements.element: Customer Data must be exported within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3(b) imposes a 30-day deadline measured from expiry or termination.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement and therefore also the fallback. The redline is not strictly minimal because it additionally triggers return and deletion of all Customer Data upon expiry or termination of any individual Order Form, even if the Agreement and other Order Forms remain active. That expansion is related but unnecessary and could disrupt continuing services. The original delivery and refund terms remain unchanged, so their commercial intent is preserved. Drafting is otherwise clear, but the overbroad Order Form trigger materially reduces quality.
